title: bug: worktree resume silently reverts tracked edits when W's index file is missing
description:
QA (qa-4b0c6c8e) found this while reviewing WT-04's reopen-1 round (task-c20464ff, completion b3b53625). That round did not cause it: the earlier 5657d186 ls-files signal does the same thing on this input.

What happens: WT-04's reuse path reads "W has no per-worktree index file" as a half-made W. It finishes W with sparse-checkout set, then `git read-tree -mu HEAD`. See moe-agent.sh provision_worktree around :2951-2967, and moe-agent.ps1 Install-MoeTaskWorktree around :2745-2760. With sparse checkout on and no index, read-tree does not refuse to overwrite a file that is already there:
- it prints `error: Path 'a.txt' already present; will not overwrite with sparse update.` for each path (git demotes the check to a warning);
- it exits 0;
- it overwrites the file with HEAD's content anyway.
Untracked new files survive. Measured on git 2.43.0 (WSL) and 2.54.0.windows.1.

End-to-end repro on Linux bash, with the WT-04 `[worktree reuse]` fixture:
1. Create W through the wrapper.
2. Edit tracked src/a.txt in W and add an untracked src/new.txt.
3. Run `rm "$(git -C W rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)"`.
4. Resume the task.
Result: `[worktree] reused`, exit 0, the CLI launches, no report_blocked. src/a.txt is back to its seed content: the edit is lost and no rescue ref holds it. new.txt survives.
Probe files: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/qa-c20464ff-r2.Wnnxai/section-idxdel.sh and driver.sh. Run `bash driver.sh <scripts snapshot root> section-idxdel.sh`.

When it can happen: something deletes W's index file (for example an agent recovering a corrupt index with `rm <index>`, then `git reset`), and the session dies before the index is rebuilt. Git itself never leaves a worktree without an index file. Exposure today is zero: worktree mode is off by default, and the CLI only moves into W with WT-05. It should land before WT-19 flips the default.

Fix direction (the planner decides): a genuine half-made W from `worktree add --no-checkout` holds nothing but its `.git` file. Finish W only when that is true. If W has no index file but holds any other entry, refuse with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED and touch nothing, so a human inspects it. That means `[ERROR]`, one report_blocked, no CLI and exit 1. Apply the same rule in both twins.
definitionOfDone: postflight case in both postflight.sh and postflight.ps1: W has no index file but holds an edited tracked file and an untracked file. The run refuses with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED: exactly one report_blocked, no CLI, exit 1. Both files keep their bytes.
A genuine half-made W, with no index file and nothing but .git, is still finished. WT-04's `[worktree reuse]` case (b) and the held-out postflight-worktree.cjs half-made case pass unchanged.
The sorted MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ token sets of moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 are identical, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.
node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash and node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell both exit 0, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

  || wtr_fail index-deleted "not exactly one report_blocked naming CREATE_FAILED"

printf 'agent edit\n' | cmp -s - "$WTR_W/src/a.txt" && printf 'agent new\n' | cmp -s - "$WTR_W/src/new.txt" \

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: QA's direction. When W has no index file, finish it only if W holds exactly one entry, `.git`. Otherwise refuse with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED and touch nothing.

Rejected:
1. `git reset` (mixed), to rebuild the index and keep W's files. After a crash in the middle of read-tree, the paths read-tree had not written yet would look like deletions, and the next landing could commit them. It would also hide a state a human should see.
2. Comparing every W file to HEAD's blob and finishing when all match. Too much code for a crash window of milliseconds, while refusing is safe.
3. Asking git (status, ls-files). With no index, git reports every path as both staged-deleted and untracked. Listing W directly is simpler and does not depend on sparse patterns.
4. `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name .git`. It works, but a Windows PATH can put FIND.EXE first. An exact compare of `ls -A` output is the shortest option and fails closed.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
